comments.author: PolyPorcupine
comments.body:
I feel it's more like the top picture if you know how to program, and the bottom one is if you don't.

While AI is better than me at finding bugs, it's also much better than me at producing them.

replies.author: Etikoza
replies.body: I’ve been coding for 20 years and Fable is making me feel like the 2nd picture. The speed at which it can understand dependencies, libraries, engines and frameworks is just insane. No human is capable of that.

replies.author: PolyPorcupine
replies.body:
It's definitely beyond any human on speed, and very similar to the transition from analog computers to digital computers, making the same mistakes faster seems like an improvement to some people.

I'm not saying it's not going to get there someday, but it's not there yet with its capabilities.

replies.author: igneus
replies.body:
I think some of what you're experiencing isn't necessarily that the foundation models themselves are getting smarter, but rather the tooling that utilises them is really starting to mature. 

I've found that good rule of thumb is that smaller models are fine for _deductive_ tasks (e.g. large codebase -> small bug list), whereas larger models like Fable are better for _inductive_ tasks (e.g. small prompt -> large codebase) There's so much focus on the latest-and-greatest nowadays that it's easy to overlook just how powerful smaller models can be when deployed in a way that maximises their utility.
